name: Symmetric Cryptography
description: Adversaries may employ a known symmetric encryption algorithm to conceal command and control traffic rather than relying on any inherent protections provided by a communication protocol. Symmetric encryption algorithms use the same key for plaintext encryption and ciphertext decryption. Common symmetric encryption algorithms include AES, DES, 3DES, Blowfish, and RC4.

strategies.name: Detection Strategy for Encrypted Channel via Symmetric Cryptography across OS Platforms

analytics.name: Analytic 0400
analytics.guidance: Processes that typically do not perform cryptographic operations loading symmetric encryption libraries (e.g., bcryptprimitives.dll, aes.dll), then initiating outbound connections with high-entropy payloads. Defender correlates process creation, DLL load, and anomalous encrypted traffic patterns.

tuning.description: Processes normally expected to use symmetric crypto (e.g., disk encryption, secure messaging).
Minimum payload entropy score for flagging unusual encrypted sessions.
Correlation window between module load and encrypted connection creation.

analytics.name: Analytic 0401
analytics.guidance: Unexpected processes (e.g., bash, python, custom binaries) dynamically loading libcrypto or performing AES/RC4 encryption operations, then initiating outbound sessions with abnormal byte entropy or asymmetric traffic patterns.

tuning.description: Baseline expected crypto libraries to suppress false positives.
Ratio of sent/received bytes indicating possible hidden C2.

analytics.name: Analytic 0402
analytics.guidance: Launchd jobs or user processes invoking symmetric crypto APIs from the Security framework and generating outbound connections carrying randomized payloads inconsistent with normal TLS patterns.

tuning.description: Legitimate DNS-over-HTTPS endpoints to avoid FP.
Define entropy level at which traffic should be flagged.

log_sources.channel: Encrypted connection with anomalous payload entropy

analytics.name: Analytic 0403
analytics.guidance: ESXi daemons (hostd, vpxa) unexpectedly using symmetric encryption routines for external connections. Defender identifies logs of service traffic with encrypted payloads inconsistent with VMware management baselines.

Defender observes NetFlow/IPFIX byte distribution anomalies or IDS/IPS detecting symmetric encryption patterns without associated key exchange.

tuning.description: Volume thresholds for distinguishing benign VPN traffic from hidden C2.
